ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the circle $\odot O$ is the incircle of $\triangle ABC$, and $\angle ABC=50^\circ$, $\angle ACB=80^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\odot O$ is the inscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $OB$ and $OC$ are the angle bisectors of $\triangle ABC$,\\
therefore $\angle OBC=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=25^\circ$, $\angle OCB=\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB=40^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BOC=180^\circ-\angle OBC-\angle OCB=\boxed{115^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, with A at the top, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; inside the triangle there is a circle tangent to the three sides, with the center of the circle labeled O; from O, lines are connected to B and C respectively, forming triangle BOC.
